extracted.intended_audience: poets, American writers, critics, and literary students interested in principles of modern/American poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for creating and assessing American poetry and literature (esp. modern/free-verse, national themes, and authenticity of voice). Emphasizes form, subject-matter, authenticity, influences, and the poet's relation to society and science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break down barriers between prose and poetry / embrace free verse
rubrics_metrics.description: The time has arrived to essentially break down the barriers of form between prose and poetry. The latter is henceforth to win and maintain its character regardless of rhyme, and the measurement-rules of iambic, spondee, dactyl, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate freeing Poetry from conventional rhyming metre; prose-poetry and freer forms better suit modern American subjects (prairies, steamships, railroads, factories, telegraphs, etc.). Rhyme and old forms had fitting roles (ballads, pensive complaints) but will no longer serve highest esthetic expression in English for American life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain natural rhythm even without strict metre
rubrics_metrics.description: The truest and greatest Poetry, (while subtly and necessarily always rhythmic, and distinguishable easily enough,) can never again, in the English language, be express'd in arbitrary and rhyming metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if abandoning formal metre and rhyme, ensure work retains an inherent, subtle rhythm that distinguishes it as poetry rather than prose. Rhythm should feel organic rather than imposed by classical metrical schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity: poems of the highest class must tally with the poet's life
rubrics_metrics.description: Of poems of the first class...they are to be sternly tallied with the poets themselves, and tried by them and their lives. Who wants a glorification of courage and manly defiance from a coward or a sneak?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-tier poems should reflect and be credible in light of the poet's character and life experience. Manufactured persona or inconsistent moral claims undermine greatness. (By contrast, lower-class poems may be manufactured without such stakes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter should engage concrete American life and national development
rubrics_metrics.description: In these States, beyond all precedent, poetry will have to do with actual facts, with the concrete States, and--for we have not much more than begun--with the definitive getting into shape of the Union. Indeed I sometimes think _it_ alone is to define the Union, (namely, to give it artistic character, spirituality, dignity.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize themes of nationality, solidarity, the dignity and heroism of practical labor (farms, factories, shipboard, mines), and the formation of democratic identity. Poetry should help counteract materialism and foster a glowing nationality and patriotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic freedom from ordinary social etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: The conventional standards and laws proper enough for ordinary society apply neither to the action of the soul, nor its poets. In fact the latter know no laws but the laws of themselves, planted in them by God, and are themselves the last standards of the law, and its final exponents--responsible to Him directly, and not at all to mere etiquette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets are permitted (and sometimes obliged) to lift the veil from social rules and explore what society forbids; the poet's duty to inner law supersedes etiquette. This freedom should be exercised responsibly (not merely to outrage gratuitously).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive polish and artificial perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: These pages are perhaps too perfect, too concentrated...it is always a make, never an unconscious growth. It is the porcelain figure or statuette...and a very choice statuette too--appropriate for the rosewood or marble bracket of parlor or library; never the animal itself, or the hunter himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor organic, living expression over highly contrived, overly refined craftsmanship that results in cold, decorative work. Anti-pattern: technically perfect writing that lacks visceral life and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize passion, imagination, and emotional depth over cold intellectuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Cold and bloodless intellectuality dominates him. ...in old or nervous or solemnest or dying hours, when one needs the impalpably soothing and vitalizing influences of abysmic Nature, or its affinities in literature or human society, and the soul resents the keenest mere intellection, they will not be sought for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should supply sustaining emotional and spiritual force, not merely abstract intellectual reason. Avoid making intellect the primary quality at the expense of feeling and imaginative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value raw, picturesque qualities over stiff propriety
rubrics_metrics.description: To the real artist in humanity, what are called bad manners are often the most picturesque and significant of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let social propriety sanitize language, gesture, or character when such roughness is more truthful or artistically effective. Picturesque irregularities can convey authenticity and vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not slavishly emulate British (anti-democratic) literary models
rubrics_metrics.description: The spirit of English literature...is almost always material, sensual, not spiritual...congests, makes plethoric, not frees, expands, dilates--is cold, anti-democratic...With the exception of Shakspere, there is no first-class genius in that literature...not models for us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of importing English/British tastes that conflict with democratic American aims; prefer models that promote expansion, freedom, and democratic sensibilities. Shakespeare is a notable exception but much else is mismatched to American needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and draw from a broad, international range of literatures
rubrics_metrics.description: American students may well derive from all former lands...from Greece and Rome...down to Italy, the German intellect...from witty and warlike France, and markedly, and in many ways, and at many different periods, from the enterprise and soul of the great Spanish race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement English/British sources with Italian, Spanish, French, German, Oriental, classical, and other traditions; good translations are essential. Diverse sources will enrich American literature and supply needed subtleties and freedoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate modern science and philosophy while re-casting older material
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest and subtlest and broadest truths of modern science wait for their true assignment and last vivid flashes of light--...priests and poets...must indeed recast the old metal, the already achiev'd material, into and through new moulds, current forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absorb discoveries (e.g., Darwinism) and modern metaphysics to inform new poetic forms and themes, but avoid letting any single scientific theory dominate all interpretation; use modern knowledge to recast traditional spiritual and poetic materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate large, appreciative audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: To have great poets, there must be great audiences, too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great poetry depends not only on individual geniuses but on the existence of broad, receptive publics; efforts to build audiences and cultural infrastructure are part of fostering poetic greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate practical labor and everyday heroism
rubrics_metrics.description: To the dignity and heroism of the practical labor of farms, factories, foundries, workshops, mines, or on shipboard, or on lakes and rivers--resumes that other medium of expression, more flexible, more eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate working-class experience, manual labor, and everyday courage as worthy poetic subjects; these subjects suit freer forms and help bind national identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve rhyme and rigid measures largely for lesser or comic effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if rhyme and those measurements continue to furnish the medium for inferior writers and themes, (especially for persiflage and the comic, as there seems henceforward, to the perfect taste, something inevitably comic in rhyme, merely in itself, and anyhow,) the truest and greatest Poetry...can never again...be express'd in arbitrary and rhyming metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhyme and fixed metrical devices can be used intentionally for light, satirical, or comic purposes, but they are generally unsuitable for highest poetic expression in modern American contexts.
